                        JOINT PETITION FOR REVIEW


      Pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Natural Gas Act, 15 U.S.C. § 717r(b), and

Federal Rule of Appellate Procedure 15(a), Petitioners Energy Alabama, Alabama

Rivers Alliance, Blackbelt Women Rising, Deep South Center for Environmental

Justice, Georgia Interfaith Power and Light, Mississippi Rising Coalition,

Ogeechee Riverkeeper, Savannah Riverkeeper, Sierra Club, Southern Alliance for

Clean Energy, Carl Moseley, and Kenny Owen (collectively, "Petitioners")

respectfully petition the United States Court of Appeals for the District of
 Columbia Circuit to review and set aside the following orders of the Federal

Energy Regulatory Commission ("Commission"):

      1.     Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company, L.L.C., Southern Natural Gas

            Company, L.L.C., Elba Express Company, L.L.C., Order Issuing

            Certificates and Approving Abandonment, 196 FERC ¶ 61,093 (July

            31, 2026) ("Authorization Order") (attached as Exhibit A); and

      2.     Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company, L.L.C., Southern Natural Gas

             Company, L.L.C., Elba Express Company, L.L.C., Notice of Denial of

            Rehearing by Operation of Law and Providing for Further •

            Consideration, 197 FERC ¶ 62,0001(Oct. 1, 2026) (attached as

            Exhibit B).

      These orders concern the Commission's issuance of the certificates of public

convenience and necessity to Tennessee Gas Pipeline, L.L.C. for the Mississippi

Crossing Project ("MSX") and to Southern Natural Gas Company, L.L.C. and Elba

Express Company, L.L.C. for the South System Expansion 4 Project ("SSE4").

One certificate authorizes Tennessee Gas Pipeline, L.L.C. to construct and operate

the MSX Project, consisting of 208 miles of new gas pipeline and appurtenant

facilities that would transport gas across Mississippi and into Alabama. The other

certificates authorize Southern Natural Gas Company, L.L.C. and Elba Express

Company, L.L.C. to construct and operate the related SSE4 Project, consisting of




                                         2
 approximately 291 miles of gas pipeline and appurtenant facilities that would

transport gas across Mississippi, Alabama, and Georgia.

      Petitioners and, in the case of those petitioners that are organizations, their

members have been and will be aggrieved by the approval, construction, and

operation of the Projects. Petitioners intervened before the Commission in the

proceedings below and timely requested rehearing of the Authorization Order. This

Petition for Review is timely because the Commission issued its Notice of Denial

of Rehearing by Operation of Law and Providing for Further Consideration on

September 30, 2026. This Court has jurisdiction and venue is proper under Section

19(b) of the Natural Gas Act, 15 U.S.C. § 717r(b).

      In accordance with Rule 15(c) of the Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure,

the list of parties served with copies of this Joint Petition for Review is attached as

Exhibit C.

                                               (Issued July 31, 2026)

        1.     On June 30, 2025, Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company, L.L.C. (Tennessee Gas)
        filed an application pursuant to section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act (NGA)1 and Part 157
        of the Commission's regulations2 for authorization to construct and operate the
        Mississippi Crossing Project (MSX Project). The project would provide approximately
        2.06 million dekatherms (MMDth) per day of incremental firm transportation service.

        2.     Concurrently, Southern Natural Gas Company, L.L.C. (Southern) and Elba
        Express Company, L.L.C. (Elba Express) jointly filed an application pursuant to
        sections 7(b) and 7(c) of the NGA3 and Part 157 of the Commission's regulations for
        authorization to construct and operate new natural gas pipeline facilities and abandon
        certain existing facilities as part of the South System Expansion 4 Project (SSE4 Project).
        The project would provide approximately 1.323 MMDth per day of incremental firm
        transportation service on Southern's existing system and 460,300 Dth per day of
        incremental firm transportation service on Elba Express' existing system.

        3.     Together, the MSX and SSE4 Projects provide a transportation path from an
        interconnection with Tennessee Gas' Line 100 in Washington County, Mississippi, to
        delivery points throughout the southeast United States. For the reasons discussed below,
        we grant the requested authorizations, subject to certain conditions.

                Background

         4.     Tennessee Gas, Southern, and Elba Express (collectively, Applicants) are
         Delaware limited liability companies and natural gas companies, as defined by
         section 2(6) of the NGA,4 engaged in the business of transporting natural gas in interstate
         commerce subject to the Commission's jurisdiction. They are affiliated through a shared
         upstream owner, Kinder Morgan, Inc. (Kinder Morgan).5 Tennessee Gas' mainline
         system extends in a northeasterly direction from Texas and Louisiana, and the Gulf of
         America, through Texas, Louisiana, Arkansas, Mississippi, Alabama, Tennessee,
         Kentucky, West Virginia, Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York, New Jersey, Massachusetts,
         New Hampshire, Rhode Island, and Connecticut. Southern's mainline system extends
         from natural gas production areas in Louisiana, Mississippi, and Alabama to markets in
         Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, and Tennessee. Elba
         Express' system is located in Georgia and South Carolina.

         IL     Proposals

         5.     The MSX and SSE4 Projects are designed to transport natural gas from western
         Mississippi to markets throughout the southeast United States. The MSX Project extends
         from an interconnection with Tennessee Gas' existing Line 100 in Washington County,
         Mississippi, to delivery points with other interstate pipelines, including Southern, in
         Mississippi and Alabama to its ultimate terminus in Choctaw County, Alabama. The
         SSE4 Project will receive gas from a new interconnection with Tennessee Gas' proposed
         MSX Project and existing receipt points on Southern's system, including an existing
         interconnection with Tennessee Gas' system. Gas will then flow eastward through
         Southern's expanded South Main Line system across Mississippi, Alabama, and Georgia
         to delivery points in Alabama and Georgia, and to the Wrens interconnection with Elba
         Express's system in Georgia, from which Elba Express will make deliveries through its
         expanded system and re-deliver a portion of the gas to Southern for further transport on
         Southern's system to end use delivery points in Georgia and South Carolina.6

                B.     SSE4 Project

         9.     The SSE4 Project consists of an expansion of Southern's South Main Line system
         and of Elba Express' system. Regarding Southern's system, the project is designed to
         provide approximately 1.323 MMDth per day of new incremental firm transportation
         service from a new interconnection with the MSX Project to delivery points in Alabama,
         South Carolina, and Georgia. Approximately 96% of the gas that would be transported
         on Southern's expanded system, or 1.272 MMDth per day, would be delivered to
         Southern at the interconnection with Tennessee Gas' MSX Project. The SSE4 Project is
         also designed to provide approximately 460,300 Dth per day of incremental firm
         transportation capacity on Elba Express' existing system. A portion of the gas
         transported on Southern's expanded South Main Line system would be delivered to Elba
         Express. That gas would either be delivered to points on Elba Express' system or
         redelivered to Southern for further transportation to delivery points in Georgia and South
         Carolina.

               A.     Certificate Policy Statement

        34. The Certificate Policy Statement provides guidance for evaluating proposals to
        certificate new construction.48 The Certificate Policy Statement establishes criteria for
        determining whether there is a need for a proposed project and whether the proposed
        project will serve the public interest. It explains that, in deciding whether to authorize the
        construction of new facilities, the Commission balances the public benefits against the
        potential adverse consequences. The Commission's goal is to appropriately consider the
        enhancement of competitive transportation alternatives, the possibility of overbuilding,
        subsidization by existing customers, the applicant's responsibility for unsubscribed
        capacity, the avoidance of unnecessary disruptions of the environment, and the unneeded
        exercise of eminent domain in evaluating new construction.

        35. Under this policy, the threshold requirement for applicants proposing new projects
        is that the applicant must be prepared to financially support the project without relying on
        subsidization from its existing customers. The next step is to determine whether the
        applicant has made efforts to eliminate or minimize any adverse effects the project might
        have on the applicant's existing customers, existing pipelines in the market and their
        captive customers, and landowners and communities affected by the new facilities. If
        residual adverse effects on these interest groups are identified after efforts have been
        made to minimize them, the Commission will evaluate the project by balancing the
        evidence of public benefits to be achieved against the residual adverse effects. This is
        essentially an economic test. Only when the benefits outweigh the adverse effects on
        economic interests will the Commission proceed to complete the environmental analysis
        where other interests are considered.
